The *Pañcahatthiyattheraapadāna* is a canonical verse text included in the *Therāpadāna* section of the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. It forms a biographical or autobiographical poetic narrative (apadāna) attributed to an elder (*thera*) named Pañcahatthiya, sharing its title with another apadāna text in the same collection (Tha-Ap 47) [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records five modern translations of the text in five languages [SuttaCentral].

According to computational analysis by DharmaNexus, the text exhibits significant Pali-internal text reuse, sharing 66 matching passages across 21 Pali texts [DharmaNexus]. Its most extensive textual overlap occurs with the first volume of the commentary to the *Theragāthā* (*Theragāthā-aṭṭhakathā*, Paṭhamo bhāgo), with 15 matching segments (the longest spanning §4.1–5.3 ↔ §2543–2546) [DharmaNexus]. It also shares standard Apadāna verse formulas with various other poems in the collection, notably *Kaṇaverapupphiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 164, §4.1–7.1 ↔ §4.1–7.1), the homonymous *Pañcahatthiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 47, §4.3–8.1 ↔ §4.3–8.1), *Naḷinakesariyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 245), and *Kaṇikārachattiyattheraapadāna* (Tha-Ap 167) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language matches with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan corpora are identified by DharmaNexus at or above a score of 10, and no external parallels are curated on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
